key_insight: AtomWorld-Mirror turns atomistic simulation into a macro-step world model that predicts physically reachable state transitions and accumulated time, instead of replaying every micro-event.
engineering_relevance: This could make long-horizon materials simulations much faster while preserving structural validity, helping engineers study diffusion, irradiation aging, defect evolution, and fracture over practical time scales.
method: Learns latent macro-step dynamics from short micro-event segments
Predicts sparse structural edits plus accumulated physical time jointly
Uses local reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency constraints
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across five atomic systems and claims 10^3 to 10^4× speedup over event-by-event simulation.
watch_item: Macro-step models may be sensitive to out-of-distribution material states or transitions, so constraint enforcement and validation on unseen regimes are important.
paper_title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
